obligations.behavior: audio.transcribe is a catalogued kind with typed params (actor, audio_path, audio_sha256, output_dir required; language, model optional) and resolves to a port under action:audio.transcribe; a non-agent actor fails actor_kind_mismatch, a base_url with credentials/query/non-http fails stt_actor_invalid
obligations.source_text: audio.transcribe is a new action kind (culture_rules/model/action_kinds.py _k entry, a port in culture_rules/node/actions/, registered as action:audio.transcribe in node/runner.py default_ports) on an agent actor whose params mirror llm.complete: base_url, model, api_key grant:..., concurrency_pool, max_concurrency; validation reuses llm.py's _base_url_problem and grant resolve

obligations.behavior: audio_path must resolve (following symlinks) inside the actor's params.audio_root and output_dir inside params.output_root; otherwise path_refused before any read or ffmpeg call; an actor with no root set refuses every path
obligations.source_text: audio.transcribe reads its audio file only under an allowlisted root set in the actor's params and refuses a path outside it or a symlink that resolves outside it (error code path_refused); nothing in culture_rules does this today, so the containment code is new (the only precedent is io/gitrepo.py:56-60, resolve() + is_relative_to)

obligations.behavior: each window is one multipart POST to base_url + /v1/audio/transcriptions with fields file and language (when given), Authorization Bearer from the grant, no proxy, no redirects; the key never appears in outputs or error messages
obligations.source_text: the upload is a multipart POST to <base_url>/v1/audio/transcriptions with the fields file and language, built with the existing encode_multipart in node/actions/library.py:123-148 (stdlib only, no new runtime dependency)

obligations.behavior: a file longer than one window yields contiguous, non-overlapping windows whose durations sum to the file's within 0.1 s, cut at a detected silence when one falls in the search span, else at the hard limit
obligations.source_text: long audio (over 600 s or 16 MiB) is split by ffmpeg on the runner host into windows under both caps, cut at silences where ffmpeg silencedetect finds one, each window sent separately, and every segment's start/end offset by its window's start; ffmpeg/ffprobe are system binaries called through subprocess argv lists (no shell, the nosec B603 convention), present on spark at /usr/bin

obligations.behavior: no window exceeds 480 s or 16 MiB as sent (16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV)
obligations.source_text: windows are re-encoded to 16 kHz mono PCM16 WAV (32 000 bytes/s), so the 16 MiB upload cap binds at about 524 s before the 600 s cap does; windows are at most 480 s long, cut earlier at a silence when one falls in the last 60 s of the window

obligations.behavior: a {text} reply becomes one segment spanning its window; a reply with segments keeps them with start/end offset by the window start; anything else fails stt_bad_response
obligations.source_text: the result file shape is {schema: 1, audio_sha256, model, language, duration, segments: [{start, end, text}], created_at}; while lobes returns only {text}, each window becomes one segment covering the window, and a later verbose_json response (lobes-cli#328) drops finer segments into the same list with no schema change

obligations.behavior: an empty window reply is kept as a segment with text ''; the file carries window_count and empty_window_count
obligations.source_text: silent gaps stay visible: a window whose reply text is empty is kept as a segment with empty text, and the result file carries window_count and empty_window_count, because lobes drops low-confidence 30 s chunks (MIN_AVG_LOGPROB) without saying so until lobes-cli#328's dropped[] ships

obligations.behavior: the result is written to a same-directory temp file then os.replace'd to <output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json; outputs are exactly result_path, result_sha256 (of the bytes on disk), audio_sha256, model, language, segment_count, window_count, empty_window_count — no transcript text
obligations.source_text: the action writes `<output_dir>/<audio_sha256>/transcript.<model-slug>.json` atomically (temp file then rename) under an allowlisted output root, and returns only scalars (result_path, result_sha256, audio_sha256, model, language, segment_count) so the transcript never sits in run state or in the rules.run.succeeded event

obligations.behavior: when the target file exists with matching audio_sha256 and model and the input audio hashes to audio_sha256, the port returns that file's outputs with zero endpoint calls and no ffmpeg run
obligations.source_text: re-running the same (audio_sha256, model) is a cheap no-op: when the result file exists and its recorded audio_sha256 and model match, the action returns the existing file's outputs without calling the endpoint

obligations.behavior: audio_sha256 not matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ fails invalid_request before any filesystem call; an audio file whose sha256 differs fails audio_mismatch before any endpoint call
obligations.source_text: audio_sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex characters (invalid_request otherwise) before it forms any path, and the action hashes the audio file and refuses a mismatch with audio_mismatch before transcribing, not only on the no-op path

obligations.behavior: per-window replies are stored atomically in a work dir keyed by (audio_sha256, model); a retried attempt sends only missing windows; the work dir is removed after the final rename
obligations.source_text: a retry resumes rather than restarts: each window's reply is kept in a work directory under the output root keyed by (audio_sha256, model), a retried attempt sends only the windows still missing, and the work directory is removed after the final rename

obligations.behavior: connection errors, 5xx, 408 and 429 fail stt_unavailable retryable; other 4xx (413 included) stt_rejected; ffmpeg/ffprobe decode failure or the endpoint's 400 invalid_audio audio_undecodable; each not retryable except stt_unavailable
obligations.source_text: failures end the run failed with distinct error codes: stt_unavailable (retryable: connection error, 5xx, 408, 429), stt_rejected (other 4xx incl. 413), audio_undecodable (ffmpeg/ffprobe or the endpoint's 400 invalid_audio), path_refused, plus the shared actor_kind_mismatch/secret_unresolved/stt_actor_invalid

obligations.behavior: ffmpeg or ffprobe missing from the node's PATH fails ffmpeg_missing, not retryable, naming the binary, before any endpoint call
